title: Open Paint Format Paint Inventory v1 (draft)
description: A portable, personal paint collection, including paints the user wants but does not have yet. Each item identifies a paint by a stable external identifier when available, or by literal fallback identity, and records a user's OWN observations (quantity, condition, storage) — distinct from global catalogue truth. Private fields are separated into a per-item `private` object and per-item `visibility`, so a shareable export profile can omit sensitive data without destructive merging. Embeds the Common document envelope. DRAFT: not frozen; see specs/inventory/v1/README.md.

items.description: The paints in the collection. MAY be empty (a collection with no items).

item.description: One paint the user owns, wants, or both. Shareable fields describe the paint and the user's holding; private fields (storage, notes, lot, acquisition) live under `private` and are omitted from a shared export.

ref.description: Document-local anchor, unique within items[] (semantic rule item-ref-unique; JSON Schema cannot express it). Across documents it is only a non-destructive duplicate-detection hint, never an identity.

owned.description: Whether the user has this paint. Absent means true, so a document written without it keeps its meaning. Only owned items count as the user's paints.

wanted.description: Whether the user intends to acquire this paint, or more of it (a wishlist or restock entry). Absent means false. Independent of `owned`.

quantity.description: How many the user owns — a user observation, not catalogue truth.

visibility.description: Default shareable. A 'private' item is omitted entirely from a shared export profile.

then.$comment: A paint the user does not have: it must be wanted (otherwise the item records nothing), and it carries none of the members that describe a bottle in hand.

privateFields.description: Sensitive, user-only fields. Removed by the shared export profile.
